page: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a multi-vCPU cloud instance positioned within the provider High Frequency Compute lineup. It features an Intel x86_64 processor delivering 12 shared vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The server is configured with 48 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources bundle 768 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results indicate balanced general-purpose throughput accompanied by specific execution strengths. In compression workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 41.11 GB/sec and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.55 GB/sec. The memory subsystem registers a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3149.22 and average cached memory bandwidth of 865.54 GB/sec. Across standard compute baselines, it maintains mid-tier performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 6682.0, PassMark CPU score of 17761.33, and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 17894.4. Application tests record steady throughput, handling 13.71 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.34 GB/sec in static web serving.

Performance tradeoffs appear primarily in uncached memory transfers and intensive machine learning tasks. Large-block uncached memory read and write speeds drop to 33.97 GB/sec and 18.41 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25 percent. In generative AI evaluations, small 135M parameter models process at average speeds, but 7B parameter LLM inference falls into the bottom quartile with 22.99 prompt tokens per second and 6.46 generation tokens per second. Because CPU allocation is shared across multi-tenant hardware, extended heavy CPU saturation may encounter variable scheduling.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 768 GB of NVMe SSD storage with 48 GB of memory provides substantial resource density without the premium of dedicated hardware. The instance fits web application hosting, CI/CD compilation pipelines, in-memory caching clusters like Redis, and transactional database deployments requiring direct fast storage.
description: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a balanced virtual server from the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 12 shared vCPUs across 6 physical Intel cores on the x86_64 architecture, 48 GB of RAM, and 768 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage. Operating at a 2.0 GHz clock rate with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it includes one public IPv4 address and lacks discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional single-threaded gzip compression and strong PassMark memory performance alongside consistent middle-tier scores across multi-core compute, Redis transactions, and static web serving. Memory bandwidth drops on large uncached blocks, and medium-scale LLM inference exhibits reduced throughput. The bundling of fast local NVMe storage with substantial memory offers solid cost efficiency for general compute without requiring dedicated core pricing. This configuration suits web serving, CI/CD pipelines, caching tiers, and relational or transactional database deployments.
